sources.title: Nissan USA newsroom: 2012 LEAF press kit
sources.notes: 2012 LEAF US press kit: SV quick charge port "-" (not offered), SL standard; 3.3 kW onboard charger; 24 kWh, 192 cells; battery heater standard on all models (a cold-weather feature, not navigation or manual preconditioning).

sources.title: Nissan USA newsroom: 2013 LEAF press kit
sources.notes: 2013 LEAF US press kit: S 3.6 kW charger (3.3 out), 6.6 kW optional; SV/SL 6.6 kW standard; quick charge port standard on SL, optional on S and SV; 24 kWh, 192 cells.

sources.title: Nissan USA newsroom: 2014 LEAF press kit
sources.notes: 2014 LEAF US press kit: S 3.6 kW charger, 6.6 kW optional; quick charge port optional on S (Quick Charge Package) and SV, standard on SL; 24 kWh, 192 cells; only cabin remote climate (CARWINGS), no battery preconditioning described.

sources.title: Nissan USA newsroom: 2016 LEAF press kit
sources.notes: 2016 LEAF US press kit: S 24 kWh, 3.6 kW charger (6.6 optional in Charge Package, which adds the quick charge port); SV/SL 30 kWh, 6.6 kW standard, quick charge port standard; battery preconditioning not mentioned (cabin only via NissanConnect EV).

sources.title: Nissan USA newsroom: 2017 LEAF press kit
sources.notes: 2017 LEAF US press kit: 30 kWh laminated Li-ion, 192 cells, "revised chemistry"; S 3.6 kW charger (6.6 kW optional via Quick Charge Package), SV/SL 6.6 kW standard; quick charge port (CHAdeMO) optional on S, standard on SV/SL; no battery preconditioning described (cabin only).

sources.title: Nissan USA newsroom: 2018 LEAF press kit
sources.notes: 2018 LEAF US press kit: 40 kWh; 6.6 kW onboard charger (6.0 out) on all trims; quick charge port optional on S, standard on SV/SL; 80 % in 40 min; battery preconditioning not mentioned (cabin only).

sources.title: Nissan USA newsroom: 2019 LEAF press kit
sources.notes: 2019 LEAF / LEAF PLUS US press kit: 40 kWh (192 cells) and 62 kWh (288 cells) laminated Li-ion; PLUS has a "standard new 100kW capacity quick charging system"; 6.6 kW onboard charger (6.0 out) on both; Quick Charge Port on both; 80 % in 40 min (40 kWh) / 45 min (62 kWh); cabin remote pre-conditioning only, nothing on battery preconditioning.

sources.title: Nissan USA newsroom: 2024 LEAF press kit
sources.notes: 2024 LEAF US press kit: S 40 kWh, SV PLUS "60 kWh" (marketing figure for the 62 kWh pack); 6.6 kW onboard charger (6.0 out); high-output quick charge port standard on both trims; 10-80 % about 40 min (S) / 60 min (SV PLUS); no battery preconditioning described.

sources.title: DOE/INL Advanced Vehicle Testing: 2013 Nissan Leaf baseline testing results (vehicle specification sheet)
sources.notes: Battery by AESC: Lithium-Ion (LMO), cathode lithium manganese oxide, 192 cells 2P96S, nominal system voltage 364.8 V, rated pack energy 24 kWh, air-cooled within a sealed pack enclosure. 2013 SV tested.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Nissan Leaf (first generation)
sources.notes: Nominal 24.15 kWh, assessed usable 21.381 kWh for the 24 kWh-class pack; standard 3.6 kW and optional 6.6 kW AC charger. No usable figure for the 30 kWh pack on the page.

sources.title: EV Database: Nissan LEAF 24 kWh (MY11-13)
sources.notes: Nominal 24 kWh, usable 22 kWh (marked estimated), NMC listed, CHAdeMO, DC max 46 kW, AC 3.3 kW standard / 6.6 kW optional, preconditioning not possible.

sources.title: EV Database: Nissan LEAF 24 kWh (MY14-17)
sources.notes: Nominal 24 kWh, usable 22 kWh (estimated), NMC listed, CHAdeMO, DC max 46 kW, AC 3.3 kW standard / 6.6 kW optional, battery preconditioning not supported.

sources.title: EV Database: Nissan LEAF 30 kWh (MY15-17)
sources.notes: Nominal 30 kWh, usable 28 kWh (estimated), NMC listed, CHAdeMO, DC max 47 kW (10-80 % average 45 kW), preconditioning not possible.

sources.title: EV Database: Nissan LEAF 40 kWh (MY18-22)
sources.notes: Nominal 40 kWh, usable 39 kWh, NMC532, nominal 350 V (400 V architecture), CHAdeMO, DC max 46 kW (Nissan claim 50 kW), AC 3.6 kW standard (EU), battery preconditioning not supported.

sources.title: EV Database: Nissan LEAF e+ 62 kWh (MY23-25)
sources.notes: Nominal 62 kWh, usable 59 kWh, NMC532, nominal 350 V, CHAdeMO, DC max 46 kW measured, AC 6.6 kW, battery preconditioning: No. MY19-22 page lists the same figures.

sources.title: Electrek: Nissan EV drivers will be able to use Tesla's Supercharger network next week (2024-12-04)
sources.notes: Only the Ariya gets Supercharger access on 2024-12-10, via a $235 CCS-to-NACS adapter; the CHAdeMO Leaf is not included.

sources.title: Nissan global newsroom: All-new 3rd generation Nissan LEAF
sources.notes: Liquid-cooled Li-ion packs 52.9 / 75.1 kWh usable; up to 150 kW DC; navigation-linked battery thermal conditioning on applicable grades; US and Canada get NACS + Plug and Charge. No chemistry or voltage named.

sources.title: Nissan Malta owner's manual: LEAF (ZE2) 2025, Li-ion battery heater
sources.notes: Third-generation LEAF (European manual): battery heater turns on automatically in the cold during DC fast charging; can be enabled while driving on the touch screen (ON/OFF/AUTO); AUTO works only during navigation route guidance and warms the battery before a fast charger.

sources.title: EV Database: Nissan LEAF Extended Range 75 kWh (MY26)
sources.notes: Usable 75.1 kWh, NMC cathode, 400 V architecture, DC max 150 kW, preconditioning supported incl. automatic via navigation (European car). AC listed 11 kW (EU three-phase), not the North American 7.2 kW.

sources.title: Electrek: Nissan LEAF reborn as a 2026 crossover with NACS (2025-06-17)
sources.notes: US spec table: S 52 kWh, S+/SV+/Platinum+ 75 kWh, all with a 7.2 kW onboard charger, 10-80 % in 35 min.

sources.title: Nissan Canada: LEAF specs
sources.notes: Lists 53 kWh and 75 kWh packs, onboard charger "7 kW and 11 kW" (not mapped to trims), 150 kW QC capacity, a battery heater.

sources.title: Nissan USA newsroom: 2023 Nissan ARIYA press kit
sources.notes: 66 kWh total / 63 kWh usable (Engage FWD, Engage e-4ORCE) and 91 kWh total / 87 kWh usable (Venture+, Evolve+, Empower+, Premiere FWD; Engage+, Evolve+, Platinum+ e-4ORCE); DC max 130 kW; 10-80 % 35 min (63) / 40 min (87) at 130 kW (the FWD table says 20-80 %); 7.2 kW onboard charger; CCS standard; liquid-cooled with battery heater; no voltage or chemistry stated.

sources.title: Nissan USA: 2023 ARIYA owner's manual (Li-ion battery warmer, EV settings)
sources.notes: Battery warmer turns on automatically when cold during quick charging, and while driving only if the "Battery Heater" setting is enabled on the touch screen; manual recommends turning it ON 30-60 min before a quick charger; setting resets OFF afterwards. No navigation trigger described. Charger limited to 130 kW.

sources.title: Nissan USA: 2025 ARIYA owner's manual (Li-ion battery warmer, EV settings)
sources.notes: Same text as the 2023 manual: manual "Battery Heater" setting (Home > Settings > EV), ON 30-60 min before a quick charger, resets OFF after quick charging; 130 kW limit; no navigation trigger.

sources.title: Nissan Canada: ARIYA specs
sources.notes: 66 kWh (63 usable) and 91 kWh (87 usable) liquid-cooled Li-ion; 7.2 kW onboard charger; 50 / 130 kW DC; lists "Quick charge port-NACS" under Mechanical AND a dealer-installed NACS Adapter Kit ($317), so the current page may describe the refreshed 2027 car; trims not mapped to packs. Nissan Canada says 35 min (63) / 40 min (87) 10-80 %.

sources.title: The Car Guide: 2026 Nissan Ariya sticks around with no changes but slashed prices
sources.notes: Canada 2026: SV FWD (ex-Engage) and SL e-4ORCE (ex-Evolve e-4ORCE) have 63 kWh; SL FWD, SL+ e-4ORCE, Platinum+ e-4ORCE have 87 kWh; no technological updates vs 2025.

sources.title: The Car Guide: Nissan releases NACS adapter for Ariya drivers (2024-12-04)
sources.notes: Canadian Ariya drivers get Tesla Supercharger access from 2024-12-10 with a Nissan adapter ($309.99); article names the 2025 Ariya; Nissan plans NACS ports on new EVs from 2025.

sources.title: EV Database: Nissan Ariya e-4ORCE 87 kWh (MY23-24)
sources.notes: 91 kWh nominal / 87 kWh usable, NMC cathode, nominal 355 V (400 V architecture), CCS, DC max 130 kW; says preconditioning supported but not automatic via navigation.

ac_max_kw.notes: Press kit: 7.2 kW onboard charger (Nissan Canada specs page also 7.2 kW).

published_10_80_min.notes: Press kit: 40 min at 130 kW (the FWD table labels it 20-80 %, the e-4ORCE table 10-80 %; Nissan Canada says "10 % to 80 % in as little as 40 minutes").

battery.preconditioning.notes: Owner's manual: battery warms automatically only when cold during quick charging; otherwise a manual "Battery Heater" setting (Home > Settings > EV) is switched ON 30-60 min before arriving; no navigation trigger described. EV Database says the European 2026 Ariya has automatic navigation preconditioning; not applicable to North American 2023-2025 cars.

charge_port.notes: Press kit: CCS charge port standard (US car); Canadian cars use the same port (adapter needed for Superchargers per Nissan Canada coverage).

supercharger_access.notes: Nissan Ariya Supercharger access from 2024-12-10 via a Nissan CCS-to-NACS adapter ($235 US, per Electrek and Nissan). Canada: adapter at $309.99 (The Car Guide names the 2025 Ariya; 2026 had "no technological updates" so assumed the same). The refreshed 2027 Canadian car is reported to get a native NACS port; not applicable here.
